messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up on the hybrid predictive + reactive autoscaler for Dedicated GPU pools. TL;DR: combine a short-horizon predictor with a fast reactive path, expose a minimal operator intent surface, and use per-tenant burst credits for fairness. Questions about config shape and rollout.
liam: +1 on hybrid. Two quick questions: predictor horizon defaults? and what's the safe max headroom we allow (cost impact)?
sasha: My vote is conservative predictor complexity initially — EWMA or short horizon AR. Predictor horizon: 30s-2m range depending on workload. Keep headroom capped at a percent of pool size (e.g. 25-50%) to bound cost.
arjun: Operator surface suggestion: expose an intent proto that contains {priority:int, max_burst_gpus:int, fallback_policy:enum, grace_ttl_secs:int}. Runtime should emit queue_depth, waiting_latency_p95, and prewarm_advice metrics.
kevin: Important: we need a concrete bursting model. Proposal: soft reservations + credit bank. Credits accrue while tenant is idle at a configured rate, capped by max_burst. Spending credits allows burst beyond reservation. Eviction only when pool fully saturated and no credits left.
maya: Agree. Add hysteresis to avoid oscillation: require sustained signal (e.g., queue_depth>threshold for N seconds) before committing scale actions. Also short cool-downs for scale-up and longer for scale-down.
sasha: Config sketch:
```
autoscaler:
  predictor:
    type: ewma
    window_sec: 30
  reactive:
    scale_up_cooldown_sec: 8
    scale_down_cooldown_sec: 60
  headroom:
    min_gpus: 1
    max_headroom_pct: 40
  fairness:
    credit_rate_per_min: 10
    max_credit_burst_gpus: 4
```
liam: Nice. A few edge cases: 1) predictor misfires (massive overpredict) — we should cap prewarm actions and rely on reactive fallback. 2) long tail jobs (batch-like) hogging GPUs — need tenant caps or soft-QoS classes.
arjun: For mispredictions, runtime should attach a trace id to prewarm/grab events so controller can reconcile prediction->allocation->utilization. That helps debugging and sim evaluations.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC doc updated -> https://drive.internal/redwood/rfc/hybrid-autoscaler (PR incoming)
kevin: Also: model variants change token-per-second and memory behavior (quantized vs fp16). Predictor should take model_variant and seq_len distribution as features.
maya: Good catch. We'll include model_variant and recent seq_len histogram in telemetry.
sasha: Monitoring: add SLOs and alerts for prediction_miss_rate (>X), burst_credit_utilization (>Y), and tenant_starvation_events. Log all fallbacks for at least 30 days.
liam: Implementation plan (rough): 1) runtime telemetry hooks (queue_depth, ttl metrics) — 2w 2) operator proto + API for intent & credits — 1w 3) predictor service + sim harness using historical traces — 2w 4) controller logic + canary rollout with traffic shaping — 2w.
arjun: Agree. For rollout: canary on small pool with synthetic bursts, then route a small percentage of real production traffic (5%) for validation. Keep rollback path simple: turn off predictor and rely on reactive path.
maya: I'll draft the operator proto and a sim dataset this week. Will also write a short experiment plan for the canary.
kevin: One more thought: quantization/variant migrations can shift latency significantly. We should emit variant-change events to the controller so it invalidates recent predictor state for that tenant.
sasha: SGTM. Also, add a debug endpoint to surface tenant credit balance and recent prewarm decisions for on-call.
liam: Can we freeze the interface by EOW? I can review the proto early tomorrow.
maya: Aim for EOW draft. I'll ping reviewers and open the PR for the operator changes.
kevin: :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks all. Follow-up: I'll attach a short sim and config diff in the PR.
